intro: Simplify a ratio, find the missing number in a proportion, or share an amount in a given ratio. Each answer comes with the working.

formula.label: Simplify a ratio
formula.expr: a : b = (a ÷ g) : (b ÷ g), where g = GCD(a, b)

formula.label: Solve a proportion
formula.expr: a : b = c : x  →  x = (b × c) ÷ a

formula.label: Share an amount
formula.expr: one part = total ÷ (a + b), shares = a × one part and b × one part

howItWorks: To simplify, the calculator finds the greatest common divisor of the parts and divides each part by it. This works for two parts or three. If you use decimals, like 1.5 : 2.5, it first multiplies every part by 10 (or 100, and so on) to make them whole numbers, then simplifies.

To solve a proportion a : b = c : x, it uses the fact that both ratios must scale by the same amount, so x = b × c ÷ a. To share an amount, it adds up the parts of the ratio, works out how much one part is worth, and multiplies back up for each person.

example.title: Sharing sweets
example.problem: Two friends share 84 sweets in the ratio 3 : 4. How many does each get?
steps: Add the parts of the ratio: 3 + 4 = 7 parts.
Check: 36 + 48 = 84, and 36 : 48 simplifies to 3 : 4 when you divide by 12.

mistakes.title: Dividing by one part instead of the total parts
mistakes.text: To share 120 in the ratio 2 : 3, divide by 2 + 3 = 5, not by 2. One part is 24, so the shares are 48 and 72.

mistakes.title: Getting the order wrong
mistakes.text: A ratio has an order. If there are 2 boys for every 3 girls, the ratio of boys to girls is 2 : 3, and girls to boys is 3 : 2.

mistakes.title: Mixing units
mistakes.text: Change both parts to the same unit first. 50 cm : 2 m is 50 : 200, which simplifies to 1 : 4, not 25 : 1.

mistakes.title: Multiplying the wrong pair in a proportion
mistakes.text: For 3 : 4 = 15 : x, the first part grew from 3 to 15, which is 5 times bigger, so x = 4 × 5 = 20. Using x = 3 × 15 ÷ 4 gives 11.25, which is wrong.

faqs.q: Can I simplify a ratio with decimals?
faqs.a: Yes. Multiply all the parts by 10, 100 or more until they are whole numbers, then simplify. For example, 1.5 : 2.5 becomes 15 : 25, which simplifies to 3 : 5.

faqs.q: How is a ratio different from a fraction?
faqs.a: A ratio compares parts with each other, and a fraction compares a part with the whole. In a class with a boys to girls ratio of 2 : 3, the boys are 2/5 of the class.

faqs.q: Can I simplify a ratio with three parts?
faqs.a: Yes. Divide every part by the GCD of all three. 12 : 18 : 30 has a GCD of 6, so it simplifies to 2 : 3 : 5.

faqs.q: What if the amount does not share out evenly?
faqs.a: The shares will be decimals. Sharing 100 in the ratio 1 : 2 gives 33.33… and 66.66…, which you may need to round depending on the question.
